Product design & delivery plan · v1.1

VeejayFoods

Order ahead. Skip the queue. A mobile pre-order and pickup app for Veejay Foods in Abuja — pay with card, bank transfer or USSD, track your order, and collect with a QR code.

Prepared 5 October 2026 · Veejay Foods · Launch area: Abuja Municipal (AMAC) · Pickup points shown (Wuse II, Garki, Jabi) are samples
Customer app (Expo / React Native) · API (Node, Express, Prisma, PostgreSQL) · Staff & admin dashboard (React)
All screenshots are captured from the real code running against the real API. Menu items, prices and customers shown are sample data.
01 · Concept

Counter queues are the problem. Pre-ordering is the fix.

2 / 19

The problem

Veejay Foods serves homemade African meals, pastries and local cuisine. Like any popular outlet in a busy city it loses sales and goodwill at peak hours: long counter queues, orders shouted over a crowd, cash handling, and “where is my order?” with no answer. Customers abandon the queue; staff get overwhelmed in bursts and idle in between.

The idea

Let customers choose a pickup point and a time slot, pay in advance, and walk in to scan a QR code. The kitchen sees a live, time-ordered queue, so demand is spread across slots instead of arriving in a rush. Money is settled before food is made, and every order has an auditable trail.

One-line promise

“Pick it, pay it, collect it — no queue.”

Launch area: Abuja Municipal (AMAC)

Pickup points are limited to Abuja Municipal Area Council districts — for example Wuse, Garki, Maitama, Asokoro, Jabi, Utako and the Central Area. Other areas and cities are out of scope for now; the data model already supports adding more pickup points later without code changes.

Why it works for each side

Customer

  • No waiting in line
  • Choose the exact pickup time
  • Pay by card, transfer or USSD
  • Live status + push notifications
  • Wrong order? Report with a photo, get refunded

Kitchen / counter

  • Orders arrive already paid
  • Slot capacity caps the rush
  • Clear New → Preparing → Ready board
  • Scan-to-collect, no disputes
  • Works for lunch and evening peaks

Owner

  • Sales by day, outlet and item
  • Sold-out toggles per outlet
  • Refund control, audit trail
  • Menu, prices and hours without a developer

Proposed success metrics

  • Median counter wait at pickup < 2 min
  • Cart → paid conversion
  • Refund rate < 2% of orders
  • Repeat orders within 14 days
Targets to agree with the business — none measured yet.

02 · Users & journey

Three people, one order

3 / 19
👩🏾‍💼

Amina — the customer

27, works in Wuse II, Abuja. Has 25 minutes for lunch, hates queues, pays by bank transfer or card on her phone. Patchy mobile data on the commute.

Needs: fast reorder, certainty about pickup time, proof of payment, a way to fix mistakes.

👨🏿‍🍳

Musa — counter staff

Runs the counter during the lunch and evening rush. Works on a shared tablet or phone, no time for menus.

Needs: one screen showing what to cook next, big buttons, a scanner that just works, a fallback when a phone dies.

👩🏽‍💼

The owner / admin

Wants to change prices, hide a sold-out dish, add a future branch, and see yesterday’s sales over breakfast.

Needs: control without a developer, trustworthy numbers, safe refunds.

The core journey (customer)

2

3

If something goes wrong

  • Paid but screen didn’t update — the app asks the server to re-check with Paystack; the webhook is the safety net.
  • Phone dies at the counter — staff type the 6-character order code instead of scanning.
  • Wrong or cold food — report in-app with a photo; admin approves and the refund goes back to the original payment method.

Design rules that follow from the users

  • A user with a paid, uncollected order is never signed out — they always have their QR.
  • Every critical button is ≥ 50 px tall; the counter UI works one-handed.
  • Prices are integers in kobo end-to-end — no rounding surprises in ₦.
  • Network failures never look like “logged out” or “payment failed”.

03 · Features

Nine capabilities, all built

4 / 19
#FeatureWhat it doesHow it was verified
1Phone + OTP sign-in6-digit SMS code (hashed, 5-min expiry, 5 attempts, rate-limited). 15-min access token + rotating 30-day refresh token. Never ends a session while an order is active.16 automated tests incl. expiry, lock-out, replay, active-order rule
2Menu & combosCategories, items, combos / meal plans with components, images, prices in ₦, per-outlet “sold out” switches.Browser-verified (app + dashboard)
3Pickup points & slotsOutlets with weekly hours (an optional “24 hours” setting exists), prep time, slot length and per-slot capacity; capacity enforced under concurrent bookings. Ready for more branches.4 + 21 tests slot maths, capacity race, hold expiry
4Cart & checkoutChoose outlet, day and time; server recomputes the price; unpaid orders hold the slot for 15 minutes, then release it.Tests + browser-verified
5Paystack paymentsHosted checkout (card, bank transfer, USSD) — card data never touches our code. Webhook verifies HMAC-SHA512, amount, currency, reference; idempotent. App can reconcile via server → Paystack verify.14 webhook tests live Paystack not yet exercised
6Order tracking + pushPlaced → Preparing → Ready → Collected, polled in-app and pushed via Expo/FCM at every change.5 state tests push not yet on a device
7QR pickupUnforgeable per-order QR (HMAC). Staff scan; only a paid, READY order at that outlet can be collected — once. Order-code fallback.Tests: forged, unpaid, double-scan, wrong outlet, race
8Complaints & refundsReport a wrong order with a photo; admin approves (full or partial) → Paystack refund to the original method → webhook finalises. Failed refunds reopen the complaint.7 tests live refund not yet exercised
9Staff & admin dashboardLive order board (with sound), QR scanner, menu / outlets / staff management, complaints & refunds, sales reports.Browser-driven against the live API

Orders are pickup-only at launch. Delivery, promo codes and loyalty are deliberately out of scope (see roadmap).

Warm, appetising, easy to tap

Canvas

Green and red are sampled from the logo itself. The pure logo shades sit at about 3.6:1 and 4:1 against white, so text and button fills use the slightly deeper variants, which clear WCAG AA (≈5.4:1 and ≈5.9:1).

Principles

  • Food first — large images, price always in green, “Add” is the loudest thing on a card.
  • State is always visible — a four-step timeline with a red ring on “now”; one status pill per order.
  • Calm money screens — one total, one button, a plain sentence about Paystack.
  • Big targets — 50 px buttons, 34 px steppers, chips instead of dropdowns for slots.
  • Honest empty/error states — tell people what happened and what to do next.

Type & spacing

System font stack (San Francisco / Roboto) for speed and native feel. Scale: 13 · 16 · 18 · 20 · 26 · 32. Spacing in 4 px steps; screens use a 16 px gutter; cards 14 px radius with a 1 px warm-grey border instead of shadows.

Brand name, logo and palette live in one theme file per surface (app, dashboard, API), so a future rebrand is a small change.
